text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- TRADE DEFICIT SHOULD HIT $2 BILLION
The February trade deficit should reach $2 billion, the worst monthly performance ever for Brazil, according to preliminary figures.
-- MORE MODERN AGRICULTURE PRODUCES RECORD HARVEST
Brazilian farmers are producing a larger crop with less funds as agriculture seeks to modernize and increase productivity.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- ECONOMY GROWS 2.91 PCT IN 1996
Brazilian gross domestic product grew 2.91 percent in 1996, according to the IBGE, boosted by growth in the agriculture and service sectors.
-- DOCUMENT CALLS FOR LEGALIZATION OF ABORTION
The Justice Ministry's women's rights council will present a petition to President Fernando Henrique Cardoso calling for the legalization of abortion.
O GLOBO
-- AGENCY OFFERS BRAZILIAN WOMEN FOR $5,000 EACH
A German agency offers Brazilian women in marriage to European men for a fee of $5,000 each.
-- TODAY IS THE DECISIVE DAY FOR RIO 2004
Today Rio de Janeiro's Olympic Committee will find out whether its bid for the 2004 games enters the final round when the IOC announces the final four to five contending cities.
-- CPI PROVES FRAUDULENT AUCTIONS BY STATES AND BROKERAGES

A special Parliamentary Investigative Committee (CPI) has received documents proving the states of Santa Catarina and Pernambuco carried out fictitious auctions of state and municipal bonds in collusion with brokerages.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
